environments.name: CI (Continuous Integration)
environments.purpose: Ephemeral, fast-feedback environment provisioned per pull request or scheduled pipeline run. Validates that every service compiles, passes unit tests, passes contract tests, and satisfies the per-service instrumentation checklist (INST-001 to INST-006). No long-lived infrastructure. All external systems are stubbed. PII scrubbing processor is active and tested.

services.tier_notes: All 23 domain/cross-cutting services and 14 platform/observability containers are instantiated. Services are started in dependency order: foundation first (SVC-100, SVC-102, SVC-105, SVC-106), then cross-cutting (SVC-050 to SVC-055), then domain (SVC-001 to SVC-017). Each service uses a lightweight in-process or Docker Compose deployment. The service dependency graph in service.yaml is the source of the startup order.

database_provisioning.persistence: None — all databases are ephemeral Docker containers (PostgreSQL:15-alpine, Redis:7-alpine for session cache). Destroyed after each pipeline run. No data survives between CI runs.
database_provisioning.seeding: Each service's CI migration scripts run at container startup. Seed data loaded from checked-in fixtures in each service's test/fixtures directory. PII fields in fixtures are synthetic (generated by Faker with UK locale). Fixture data schema must be validated against the service's domain model before the pipeline passes.

secrets.source: Environment variables injected by CI runner (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI secrets). Short-lived, single-use secrets generated per pipeline run.
secrets.rotation_policy: CI secrets are ephemeral — they expire at the end of the pipeline run. No rotation policy needed. DB passwords are randomly generated per run by Docker Compose.
secrets.pci_dss_keys: Test encryption keys only — pre-generated RSA-2048 key pairs checked into the CI test fixtures repository under git-crypt. These keys must NEVER be used outside CI. CI-only flag enforced by OPA policy gate.
secrets.notes: SVC-105 (HashiCorp Vault) runs in dev mode in CI (no HSM, in-memory storage). Dev mode is blocked from RC and Prod-Parity environments by a CI pipeline OPA policy gate that checks VAULT_DEV_MODE=false.

otel_config.collector_deployment: Single OTel Collector sidecar per service in Docker Compose. No gateway collector in CI — each service's collector is standalone. PII scrubbing processor is active and validated by a CI test that asserts PII fields are absent from emitted telemetry.

exporters.retention: CI run duration only — Loki container destroyed after run
exporters.notes: Loki single-container in Docker Compose. Used to validate structured log schema (INST-001) against LOG-CAT-00X schema checks.
Tempo single-container. Used to validate W3C TraceContext propagation (INST-002) across service calls in integration tests.
Prometheus in Docker Compose. Validates RED metrics emission (INST-003) and health endpoint format (INST-004).

Audit Store is NOT active in CI. Audit log schema compliance is validated by a contract test asserting the audit event payload shape, but no WORM store is provisioned. This avoids accumulating test data in the 7-year WORM store.

otel_config.sampling_strategy: 100% sampling in CI — all traces and logs captured to maximise test failure visibility.
otel_config.audit_store: Disabled in CI. Contract tests validate audit event schema only.

network_zones.implementation: All containers on a single Docker Compose network. No zone enforcement in CI. Network zone policies are validated by static analysis of Istio AuthorizationPolicy manifests in CI, but not runtime-enforced.

environments.name: RC (Release Candidate)
environments.purpose: Persistent, production-like release candidate environment. Used for end-to-end integration testing, regression testing, performance baseline measurement, security scanning, and UAT. External systems are primarily stubbed but production-equivalent stubs (contract-verified). Full OTel stack active. Secrets rotated on a schedule. Network zones enforced by Istio.

services.tier_notes: All services deployed as Kubernetes Deployments on a shared RC Kubernetes cluster (separate from production namespace). Tier ordering enforced by Kubernetes Init Containers and readiness probes: foundation services must be Ready before cross-cutting services start, cross-cutting before domain. Deployment manifests are production-equivalent. Resource limits mirror production within 80% to allow RC cluster cost savings.

database_provisioning.persistence: Persistent Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaims backed by managed cloud storage (AWS EBS gp3 / Azure Premium SSD). Data persists across deployments. RC databases are NOT destroyed between releases — regression test baseline data is preserved.
database_provisioning.seeding: Initial seeding from checked-in synthetic fixtures on first cluster provision. Subsequent runs use the accumulated RC dataset (reset on a monthly basis via a seeding job). Anonymised production-like dataset volumes are used for performance baseline tests (min 100k retail accounts, 10k SME accounts, 500k payment records, 50k fraud cases).

secrets.source: HashiCorp Vault Enterprise (RC instance, separate from production Vault cluster). Service accounts use Kubernetes auth method — Vault issues short-lived tokens to service accounts presenting their K8s service account JWT.
secrets.rotation_policy: Database dynamic secrets: 4-hour TTL (Vault database engine). TLS certificates: 7-day TTL (Vault PKI engine, auto-renewed by cert-manager at 70% of TTL). API keys for external stubs: rotated weekly via Vault static secret rotation. PCI DSS encryption keys: rotated every 180 days in RC (matches the production 365-day policy at half-frequency for testing rotation procedures).
secrets.pci_dss_keys: HSM-backed AES-256 encryption keys for PCI CDE-scoped services (SVC-003, SVC-008, SVC-011) provisioned in the RC Vault cluster with a software HSM emulator (not a physical HSM). Physical HSM is production-only. RC PCI keys are flagged as non-production in Vault metadata.
secrets.notes: Secrets access is logged to the RC Audit Store. Secret access metrics (secret_age_days, expiry countdown) are exported to the RC Metrics Store and displayed on the Grafana observability dashboards.

otel_config.collector_deployment: OTel Collector deployed as a DaemonSet (one Collector pod per Kubernetes node) plus a Collector gateway deployment (2 replicas, HPA enabled). Sidecar mode is used only for SVC-003, SVC-008, SVC-011 (PCI CDE namespace — DaemonSet is excluded from CDE namespace for blast radius containment).

exporters.retention: 90 days hot, 30-day tier to cold object storage
exporters.notes: Loki deployed as a Kubernetes StatefulSet with S3 backend for long-term log storage. RC log data persists for 90 days for regression analysis.
Grafana Tempo with S3 backend. Full p99 latency baseline established from RC traces before each production release.
Prometheus with Grafana Mimir long-term storage. 13-month retention established in RC before production to validate Mimir compaction and query performance.

RC Audit Store is a separate S3 Object Lock bucket in the RC AWS account. WORM is active (Compliance mode). RC audit data contributes to the regulatory evidence trail if RC is used for regulated workflow testing (e.g. sanctions screening regression tests). RC audit store is NOT shared with production.

otel_config.sampling_strategy: Head-based sampling at 20% for high-volume services (SVC-009, SVC-011, SVC-013) to manage trace storage cost. 100% sampling for all error spans (always-on error sampling). 100% sampling for regulated event types (payment sanctions screening, fraud decisions, KYC clearance).
otel_config.audit_store: Active WORM S3 bucket in RC AWS account. Separate from production audit store. Cryptographic sealing active (Vault-backed HMAC key). Auditor access requires approved change request.

network_zones.implementation: Istio IngressGateway in dedicated namespace with NodePort → LoadBalancer. WAF (AWS WAF or Cloudflare) in front of IngressGateway. NetworkPolicy blocks direct pod-to-pod access from DMZ to Application Zone.

Istio AuthorizationPolicy STRICT mode on all service namespaces. mTLS STRICT mode on all Pods. Zero-Trust Policy Map applied (deny-all baseline with explicit allow entries). Kubernetes NetworkPolicy as defence-in-depth.

Dedicated pci-cde Kubernetes namespace with dedicated NodePool (dedicated EC2/VM instances, not shared with non-PCI workloads). Istio AuthorizationPolicy: only SVC-001, SVC-013, SVC-052 may ingress to PCI CDE namespace. Kubernetes NetworkPolicy: egress to card networks only via allow-listed IP ranges.

Kafka cluster accessible only from Application Zone namespaces (Kubernetes NetworkPolicy on Confluent Cloud / MSK VPC peering). PostgreSQL instances in private subnets, accessible only via Vault dynamic secret + VPC Security Group.

Audit Store bucket policy denies all except dedicated OTel Collector OTLP exporter IAM role (write-only) and auditor IAM role (read-only via bastion). Vault (SVC-105) in dedicated Compliance Zone VPC with VPC peering to Application Zone only.
Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo deployed in dedicated monitoring namespace. Health probe access to all namespaces via Kubernetes NetworkPolicy allow rules. VPN-required for SRE access to Grafana.

environments.name: Prod-Parity (Production Parity)
environments.purpose: Production-equivalent environment used for final pre-release validation, disaster recovery drills, penetration testing, regulatory evidence collection under OPRES (Operational Resilience), and capacity planning. Identical Kubernetes node types, network topology, secrets management (physical HSM), and OTel pipeline to production. External systems use production sandbox APIs where available, or production-grade stubs with network characteristics matching production latencies.

services.tier_notes: Same Kubernetes node types (e.g. AWS c6i.4xlarge for compute, r6i.2xlarge for data-intensive services). Same replica counts as production. Same HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) configurations. Same Istio version and configuration. Prod-Parity is used for: chaos engineering (Chaos Mesh), performance soak tests, FCA operational resilience impact tolerance testing, and pre-release sign-off by the CTO/CISO.

database_provisioning.persistence: Multi-AZ managed database instances (AWS RDS Multi-AZ / Azure SQL Hyperscale) matching production database tier. Automated backups enabled (35-day retention). Point-in-time recovery tested quarterly as part of DR drills.
database_provisioning.seeding: Production-equivalent synthetic dataset: 5 million retail accounts, 500k SME accounts, 100k corporate accounts, 50 million payment records, 5 million card transaction records, 500k fraud cases. Dataset generated by a reproducible synthetic data generation pipeline (Gretel AI or Faker with UK locale). No real customer data — UK GDPR prohibits use of real personal data in non-production environments without explicit consent and DPIA.

secrets.source: HashiCorp Vault Enterprise with physical HSM (AWS CloudHSM or Thales Luna) — same HSM tier as production. Kubernetes auth method. All service accounts present K8s service account JWTs to Vault for token issuance.
secrets.rotation_policy: Database dynamic secrets: 1-hour TTL (same as production). TLS workload certificates: 24-hour TTL (same as production). API keys: rotated every 30 days. PCI DSS encryption keys: rotated every 365 days (production policy, tested at full frequency in Prod-Parity). Secret rotation is tested in Prod-Parity as part of quarterly DR drills — a forced rotation is triggered while services are under load to validate zero-downtime rotation.
secrets.pci_dss_keys: Physical HSM-backed AES-256 keys for SVC-003, SVC-008, SVC-011 (PCI CDE). AWS CloudHSM cluster in PCI CDE VPC. FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified. Key ceremony documented and performed by CISO and auditor. PCI DSS Requirement 3.6 key custodian records maintained in Audit Store.
secrets.notes: Vault telemetry (secret access counts, expiry metrics, PKI utilisation) exported to OTel Collector → Metrics Store → Grafana. Secret expiry alerts (FRS-005) tested in Prod-Parity by deliberately setting a test secret to expire in 72 hours and verifying the alert fires.

otel_config.collector_deployment: OTel Collector DaemonSet (one per node) plus dedicated Collector gateway (3 replicas, HPA up to 10). Collector gateway is in a dedicated observability namespace. Sidecar Collectors in PCI CDE namespace (DaemonSet excluded from PCI namespace). Collector configuration identical to production.

exporters.retention: 90 days hot, tiered to S3 cold after 30 days
exporters.notes: Loki production-equivalent configuration: 3-node StatefulSet, S3 backend with Loki compactor. Log ingestion rate tested at production peak: ~500k log lines/second across all services.
Grafana Tempo production configuration. Trace ingestion at production-equivalent load (100k spans/second at peak) tested during capacity planning runs.
Grafana Mimir production-equivalent configuration. Long-term compaction tested. SLO dashboards verified at full cardinality.

Prod-Parity Audit Store is a separate WORM S3 bucket in the Prod-Parity AWS account (NOT the production audit store). S3 Object Lock Compliance mode active. Cryptographic sealing via HSM-backed HMAC key. Auditor access two-person control tested quarterly. Completeness check (FRS-007) active: alert if audit event volume drops >30% below 4-week rolling average.

otel_config.sampling_strategy: Same as production: 10% head-based sampling for high-volume services (SVC-009, SVC-011, SVC-013). 100% for error spans. 100% for regulated transactions (sanctions, fraud, KYC, credit). Tail-based sampling enabled for traces with p99 latency > 2× SLO to capture outliers for performance investigations.
otel_config.audit_store: Active WORM S3 Object Lock Compliance mode bucket in Prod-Parity AWS account. Physical HSM-backed cryptographic sealing (SHA-256 HMAC). Auditor-only access (two-person control, AWS IAM Permission Boundary). Quarterly access control test (negative test asserting engineer role deletion attempt is denied).

network_zones.implementation: Same as production: AWS WAF + Shield Advanced in front of NLB → Istio IngressGateway. DDoS attack simulation tested quarterly as part of operational resilience testing. Ingress controller in dedicated dmz namespace — no co-residency with application workloads.

Istio AuthorizationPolicy STRICT on all application namespaces. mTLS STRICT mode enforced — zero PERMISSIVE pods. Zero-Trust Policy Map identical to production. Chaos Mesh fault injection used for blast radius testing: a simulated SVC-013 compromise tests whether lateral movement to SVC-001 or SVC-051 is prevented by the policy map.

Dedicated PCI Kubernetes NodePool on dedicated EC2 instances (no shared node co-residency). Istio AuthorizationPolicy: explicit deny-all for non-PCI-scoped services. Kubernetes NetworkPolicy layer-2 defence. QSA-reviewed network segmentation diagram validated against live Prod-Parity configuration.

Confluent Cloud dedicated cluster in private VPC (AWS PrivateLink). RDS Multi-AZ instances in private subnets — no public endpoint. VPC Security Groups: only Application Zone pods may reach database port 5432 via Vault dynamic credentials. Network flow logs exported to SVC-103 (Audit & Logging).

WORM Audit Store bucket policy: write-only from OTel Collector OTLP exporter IAM role; read-only from auditor bastion IAM role. Vault HSM cluster in dedicated Compliance Zone VPC — no direct access from Application Zone; all Vault requests via Vault agent sidecar with Kubernetes auth. Management access via VPN + hardware MFA.

Observability stack (Grafana, Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Prometheus) in dedicated monitoring namespace. VPN + hardware MFA required for SRE access. Prometheus health probe NetworkPolicy allow-rules identical to production. Grafana dashboards tested at production equivalent cardinality.
